findings.highlight: My vision and perception is filled with black
findings.evidenceJa: 視界と知覚が、黒一色に染め上げられた
findings.governingReading: Both vision and perception are dyed entirely black.
findings.explanation: The coordinated plural subject is paired with singular “is,” producing a grammatical error at the onset of the injury sequence.

findings.highlight: “Oh[line4]”
findings.evidenceJa: 「ぁ[line4]」
findings.governingReading: Shirou emits a faint, broken “ah.”
findings.explanation: The English changes an involuntary strained sound into the lexical interjection “Oh.”

findings.highlight: [blank page]
findings.evidenceJa: 熱い。
findings.governingReading: The centered isolated beat states only “Hot.”
findings.explanation: The English page is blank, deleting the first discrete sensation in the alternating perception sequence.

findings.highlight: [blank page]
findings.evidenceJa: ない。
findings.governingReading: The centered isolated beat states “Nothing” or “Gone.”
findings.explanation: The English page is blank, deleting the second step in Shirou’s fragmentary realization.

findings.highlight: a black sun must have come falling down
findings.evidenceJa: 黒い太陽でも落ちてきたのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether even a black sun has fallen, using comparison to explain clearly perceived darkness.
findings.explanation: The English turns his speculative question into a necessary conclusion.

findings.highlight: [blank page]
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=じぶん]体が、ない。
findings.governingReading: The centered line writes “body” and reads it as “self”: his body—he himself—is gone.
findings.explanation: The English page is blank, deleting both the perception and the body/self ruby relation.

findings.highlight: It probably melted from the heat.
findings.evidenceJa: 太陽の熱で溶かされたのだ
findings.governingReading: In his dazed reasoning, his body was surely melted by the sun’s heat.
findings.explanation: The English removes the black-sun image from the cause and weakens the thought’s conviction.

findings.highlight: I flail my right arm to drive it off.
findings.evidenceJa: 右腕で懸命に抗った
findings.governingReading: Shirou desperately resists the shadow with his right arm.
findings.explanation: The English replaces effortful resistance with ineffectual flailing and invents the goal of driving the shadow away.

findings.highlight: Embracing her with that same arm, I press her to the ground.
findings.evidenceJa: イリヤの体を右手で抱いて、とにかく地面に張り付いた
findings.governingReading: Holding Illya with his right hand, Shirou clings to the ground at all costs.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the pressing action to Illya instead of Shirou anchoring himself while holding her.

findings.highlight: All I lost was my left arm.
findings.evidenceJa: なくなったのは、左肩の向こうだけ
findings.governingReading: Everything beyond Shirou’s left shoulder is gone.
findings.explanation: The English regularizes the catastrophic boundary into the simpler loss of an arm.

findings.highlight: It vanished without trace.
findings.evidenceJa: じゅっ、と音をたててキレイさっぱり消え去った
findings.governingReading: The missing part vanishes cleanly with a brief sizzling sound.
findings.explanation: The English preserves disappearance but deletes its only immediate sound.

findings.highlight: That’s the only part of me that vanished without trace. The rest of my body is still there.
findings.evidenceJa: 体はちゃんと残っている。残っている。
findings.governingReading: Shirou repeats that his body remains, remains, as shock-driven reassurance.
findings.explanation: The English adds a second explanatory pair after already translating the same propositions, turning deliberate repetition into accidental duplication.

findings.highlight: I only lost one of the two.
findings.evidenceJa: 大きく何かが欠けてしまった
findings.governingReading: Something immense has gone missing, enough to feel as though his whole body vanished.
findings.explanation: The English invents an unexplained division into two and reduces the magnitude to “only” one part.

findings.highlight: its energy spent
findings.evidenceJa: 今ので力を使い果たしたのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou conjectures that the shadow may have exhausted its power with the preceding action.
findings.explanation: The English states the proposed explanation as fact.

findings.highlight: My ears must be numb, as I can’t hear what she’s saying.
findings.evidenceJa: 耳が麻痺したのか、何を言っているのか、よくわからない
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether his hearing is numb because he cannot make out what Illya is saying.
findings.explanation: The English makes the suspected cause certain and changes difficulty understanding into inability to hear.

findings.highlight: This body is almost dead anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: この体は限界だ
findings.governingReading: Archer says his body has reached its limit.
findings.explanation: The English converts functional exhaustion into a near-death diagnosis.

findings.highlight: it will not make a difference even if my arm is cut off
findings.evidenceJa: これを呉れてやったところで変わるまい
findings.governingReading: Archer says that if he is disappearing anyway, giving this to Shirou will change nothing.
findings.explanation: The English replaces voluntary transplantation with the passive event of Archer’s arm being cut off and leaves the recipient unstated.

findings.highlight: I give this away.”
findings.evidenceJa: これを呉れてやったところで変わるまい
findings.governingReading: Archer’s sentence ends inside one continuous quotation with his offer to give the limb.
findings.explanation: The English closes the quotation early, then leaves a second first-person sentence outside it with an unmatched closing quote.

findings.highlight: the boy and I are an exception
findings.evidenceJa: オレとその男は特例だ
findings.governingReading: Archer calls himself and “that man” exceptions.
findings.explanation: The English changes Archer’s distanced adult designation of Shirou into “the boy.”

findings.highlight: He tenderly runs his fingers through Tohsaka’s hair.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の髪を、一度だけ、愛しげに梳いていた
findings.governingReading: Archer tenderly combs through Rin’s hair only once.
findings.explanation: The English omits the one-time limit that gives the farewell gesture its restraint.

findings.highlight: The dark sun no longer shines on the forest.
findings.evidenceJa: 森に黒い太陽はもうない
findings.governingReading: The black sun is no longer present in the forest.
findings.explanation: The English implies that the sun remains but has stopped shining, weakening Shirou’s distinction between the vanished phenomenon and failing consciousness.

findings.highlight: The darkness must be falling on my consciousness.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の意識に、暗い闇が落ちてきたのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether dark darkness is now falling over his consciousness.
findings.explanation: The English again converts his disoriented question into a necessary conclusion.

findings.highlight: a voice that sounds just like mine
findings.evidenceJa: 俺みたいな声
findings.governingReading: Archer’s voice sounds like Shirou’s.
findings.explanation: “Just like” strengthens resemblance into near identity during a deliberately restrained clue.

findings.highlight: bids farewell
findings.evidenceJa: [ruby text=わかれ char=2]別離を告げていた
findings.governingReading: Archer announces a written “separation” read as “farewell.”
findings.explanation: The English retains only the spoken reading and loses the written layer emphasizing permanent parting.
